description:
Two records are read and displayed, and then CLOSE at :138 reports '42'. The pair is chosen for a property no other case in this program pins: across it the base key and the customer/account ids are ANTI-CORRELATED. Line 1 of app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt carries the LOWEST XREF-CARD-NUM of all fifty rows, 0500024453765740, together with the HIGHEST XREF-CUST-ID, 000000050, and the highest XREF-ACCT-ID, 00000000050; line 49 carries a near-highest base key, 9680294154603697, which ranks 49th of 50, together with the LOWEST of both ids, 000000001 and 00000000001. app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl:30-32 declares ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED, ACCESS MODE IS SEQUENTIAL and RECORD KEY IS FD-XREF-CARD-NUM, and the browse runs over the CCXREF base KSDS - app/jcl/READXREF.jcl:25-26 binds //XREFFILE to the base cluster and never to the CXACAIX alternate-index path over it - so the one correct read order is ASCENDING XREF-CARD-NUM, line 1 and then line 49, even though that is DESCENDING customer and account id. An implementation that browsed the alternate-index path, or that ordered on XREF-CUST-ID or on XREF-ACCT-ID, would emit these two records the other way round and fail here, which is what makes this case a guard on gate G45 - the alternate index is an additional access path over one cluster, never a second table and never a reordering - as well as on read order. Everything after the record lines is the close failure: 9000-XREFFILE-CLOSE takes its :141 arm, ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at :142, and :147-150 run, so RETURN-CODE is 12 and there is NO 'END OF EXECUTION OF PROGRAM CBACT03C' line at all, because :150 abends before :85 can be reached. '42' is numeric and its IO-STAT1 is '4', so 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS takes its ELSE arm at :170-172 and renders NNNN0042, where case13 reaches the extended arm from this same paragraph. The close paragraph also writes its APPL-RESULT arithmetic the long way round - ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING at :137 and SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT at :140, where the open paragraph uses plain MOVEs - and the values are identical either way. Each record still appears TWICE and consecutively, because DISPLAY CARD-XREF-RECORD is active at :96 inside the '00' arm of 1000-XREFFILE-GET-NEXT and again at :78 in the mainline loop; that doubling is a defect practice B5 forbids tidying, so two records produce four record lines and eight lines in total. The two rows are seeded at the 36 characters the shipped data actually measures, and CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 supplies CVACT03Y's absent FILLER PIC X(14) at seed time rather than the case pre-padding it. Every expected value here is STATICALLY DERIVED - never captured from an execution of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment (AAP risk R-A) - by structured reading of app/cbl/CBACT03C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy, app/jcl/READXREF.jcl and app/data/ASCII/cardxref.txt, none of which may be edited to make a difference go away.

HOW THE FAULT IS INDUCED, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. This case arranges a failed CLOSE: unitStimulus.callSiteOutcomes names the call site CLOSE-XREFFILE and gives it FILE STATUS '42'. It is declared here because the identifier of a case must never configure it - a table in Java keyed by 'case01'..'case20' meant this file described three abend lines with nothing in it to say why, and renumbering a case silently changed what it did. A case that declares no call-site outcome runs clean, so silence here is itself a statement.
